# Enemy force fields scale with level progression

**Headline:** Add data-driven enemy force fields that appear from a per-archetype
start level (some enemies shielded from level 2, others later) and grow stronger
with each level, absorbing a number of player hits before the ship inside is
exposed and destroyed as normal.

## Problem statement

Deeper campaign levels currently raise threat only through raw enemy density and
firepower; each regular enemy is still a single-hit (or fixed 5-hit) target. The
result is that upgraded weapons trivialise late-level fodder. Adding a
**force-field layer** — a distinct, readable barrier that absorbs several hits
before the ship inside becomes vulnerable — gives the late campaign a new
escalation axis that existing durability (`EnemyConfig.health`) does not provide,
without touching weapon/power-up economies.

## Users

- **As a player**, I want enemies in deeper levels to absorb a few hits behind a
  visible barrier, so late-game firepower is challenged again and reading a
  shielded enemy (barrier first, hull second) is intuitive.
- **As a balance engineer**, I want force-field strength (which archetypes are
  shielded, from which level, and how the field's hit count grows) to be
  data-driven and tunable per enemy, so I can shape difficulty without scene
  code.
- **As a developer**, I want the force-field logic to live once in the shared
  core so the game and every gym behave identically, with no divergent copies.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Data-driven per-archetype fields.** New `EnemyConfig` fields
  `forceFieldStartLevel` (campaign level at which this archetype first gains a
  field; `0` = never shielded), `forceFieldStartHits` (field hits when it
  appears) and `forceFieldMaxHits` (field hits at the campaign maximum level)
  are added to the CSV schema/codec, config types and seed defaults, each
  defaulting so that **every existing enemy is unshielded at level 1** and the
  shipped campaign is behaviourally unchanged until at least level 2. Field
  strength at any level is `clamp(round(lerp(startHits @ startLevel → maxHits @
  10)), 0, 5)` via a pure, Phaser-free shared resolver. Heavier archetypes
  (Tank/Harvester) carry higher base values than light ones.
- **AC2 — Force-field absorbs hits before the hull.** A shielded enemy survives
  its fleet of field hits first; each absorbed hit consumes the bullet (with
  feedback) but does **not** decrement `EnemyConfig.health`. Only after the
  field is broken does the enemy's normal health apply (so most archetypes die
  on the next hit; the 5-HP Harvester still needs 5). Every player damage source
  (normal bullet, piercing, AOE weapons, Smart Bomb, Orbital Strike, Frenzy
  bonus hits) depletes the field through the existing shared `takeDamage()`
  seam — no parallel damage path. Player contact/ram: a shielded enemy's field
  absorbs the ram — exactly one field hit is consumed, the enemy survives, the
  player survives the collision and is not destroyed. Once the field is down,
  the existing contact rule applies unchanged (both destroyed,
  AH-0MTV7JOLU006W8PT). The absorb must be one field hit per ram contact, not
  per overlapping frame (documented re-arm, mirroring the Thorn Field ram
  absorption in `CombatScene._handleCollisions` step 4).
- **AC3 — Readable feedback.** Shielded enemies render a shared bubble drawn by
  the `CombatEffectVisuals` helper family, visually distinct from the player's
  Shield and Force Field bubbles; each absorbed hit triggers the existing shared
  impact feedback; the breaking hit runs a distinct break flash/audio cue.
- **AC4 — Gym parity and tunability.** The same resolver drives the game
  (`PlayScene` spawn path, run level from `WaveManager`) and the level gym
  (`GymLevel`), with a parity test. The enemy-config gym editor
  (`GymFodderEnemies` slider surface) gains force-field controls so a
  formation-gym (no campaign context) spawn can force a field on with a given
  hit count; the divergence (gym slider sets hits directly instead of a level
  curve) is recorded in the code and this item.
- **AC5 — Verification and documentation.** Unit tests cover the resolver curve
  (start level, ramp, clamping, cap, L1-unchanged), CSV codec defaults, entity
  absorb/break behaviour, and scene integration; game↔gym parity test passes;
  the duplicate-body guard stays green; a bot-batch evidence run at L1/L5/L10
  records `survivalSeconds`, `levelReached`, `avoidableHits` and
  `enemiesKilledByArchetype` before/after (or demonstrates the field keeps the
  campaign playable). GDD §2.6 (remove "no shield layer"), §4.1 and
  `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` are updated with the new behaviour
  and tuning table; **all related documentation is updated** and the **full
  project test suite passes** with the changes.

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity is mandatory** (repo `AGENTS.md`): enabled gameplay
  behaviour is shared code consumed by the game and every relevant gym; only a
  documented disabled feature may diverge. The force-field resolver and bubble
  helper must live in the shared core, not per-scene copies.
- **Level 1 is untouched.** Defaults guarantee zero shielded enemies at level 1,
  preserving onboarding, tests and the existing balance baseline.
- **No changes to enemy `health`, weapon/power-up economies, or the player
  Force Field / Shield power-ups.** Fields are a new, additive layer.
- **Backwards-compatible config persistence** — existing enemy config blobs and
  the CSV load with the new fields defaulted (`0`); no schema break.
- **Determinism** — field strength is a pure function of (level, config); same
  level + seed ⇒ identical shields, so the fixed/curve campaign determinism
  contract is preserved.
- **No new player-facing UI** beyond the in-game bubble and gym editor controls.

## Existing state

- Regular-enemy health is data-driven (`EnemyConfig.health`, default 1; Harvester
  5 HP) and applied via `BaseEnemy.takeDamage()` — the shared damage seam every
  damage source already routes through (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`:
  bullet, piercing, AOE, Smart Bomb, Orbital Strike, Frenzy).
- `EnemyConfig` is CSV-backed (`src/data/enemy-configs.csv`) with a numeric
  codec (`src/core/csv.ts`), seed defaults (`src/core/configDefaults.ts`) and a
  **gym enemy editor** slider surface (`GymFodderEnemies.ENEMY_SLIDER_RANGES`).
- Spawn seam: `PlayScene._spawnEnemy` → `loadEnemyConfig(key)` →
  `createEnemyFromConfig`; the run level is available via `WaveManager.level`.
  `GymLevel` launches real campaign waves through the same factory.
- The **player** has Shield (absorbs hits) and Gradius-style Force Field
  (reflects bullets) power-ups; neither has any enemy-side counterpart. GDD
  §2.6 currently states "no shield layer", which this feature deliberately
  changes.
- Level-scaling work is in flight (epic AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P): its contract tests
  (AH-0MVLJCYGW001TRB3) are done; the `src/core/levelScaling.ts` implementation
  (`AH-0MVLJEE7O008RX9X`) is pending.

## Desired change

1. Add `forceFieldStartLevel` / `forceFieldStartHits` / `forceFieldMaxHits` to
   `EnemyConfig` (types, CSV codec, seed defaults, CSV rows; default 0/1/1).
2. Add a pure resolver (proposed `src/core/enemyForceField.ts`,
   `enemyForceFieldHits(level, config)`); coordinate reuse of
   `levelScaling.ts` plumbing if F1 (AH-0MVLJEE7O008RX9X) has landed.
3. Thread the resolved field hits into entity spawn (game and level gym through
   the shared factory/config path) and implement field state + bubble in
   `BaseEnemy` (draw, absorb decrement, break effects); keep `takeDamage()`
   consuming the field before `health`. Add the **ram-absorb branch** to
   `CombatScene._handleCollisions` step 4 (one field hit per ram contact,
   player and enemy both survive; falls through to the existing both-destroyed
   rule once the field is down) — shared, so the game and every gym inherit it.
4. Add the shared bubble/break visuals to `CombatEffectVisuals` and any new SFX
   cue to the audio registry; add the gym-editor force-field sliders.
5. Tests: TDD contract tests for the resolver/codec/entity, game↔gym parity,
   and a bot-batch evidence run at L1/L5/L10.
6. Update GDD §2.6/§4.1 and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`; refresh
   the enemy-config CSV header comments.

## Key Files

- `src/core/configTypes.ts` — Add `forceFieldStartLevel`, `forceFieldStartHits`, `forceFieldMaxHits` to `EnemyConfig`.
- `src/core/configDefaults.ts` + `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` — Seed defaults and per-archetype values (`0` default = never/unchanged).
- `src/core/csv.ts` — Numeric codec support for the new columns (default 0).
- `src/core/enemyForceField.ts` — **New** pure resolver `enemyForceFieldHits(level, config)` (curve, clamp, cap 5, L1 = 0).
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` — Field state, bubble draw, absorb-before-health in `takeDamage()`, break feedback, ram-absorb entry point.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` (+ `CombatScene.test.ts`) — Ram-absorb branch in `_handleCollisions` step 4 with the shared re-arm, mirroring `tryConsumeThornsRam`. Note: this file is **shared core**, so the change lands once for the game and all gyms.
- `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts` — Thread effective field hits into entity construction from config.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — Resolve and pass field hits at spawn (run level via `WaveManager`).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts` (+ `GymBotTuning`/`GymCurveSequencer` if they spawn campaign waves) — same resolver for parity.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymFodderEnemies.ts` — Force-field sliders/controls on the enemy-config editor (documented divergence: direct hits, no level curve).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatEffectVisuals.ts` (+ tests) — Shared enemy-force-field bubble + break flash helper.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — Any field-break cue (reuse existing cues where possible).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — Game↔gym parity block stays green.
- `src/core/*.test.ts`, `src/entities/BaseEnemy.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/*.test.ts` — Resolver, codec, entity, integration tests.
- `src/ai/eval/` + `scripts/evaluate.mjs` — Bot-batch evidence mode at L1/L5/L10 (extend the F5 per-level harness if landed).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — Behaviour + tuning table.

## Related work

- **AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P** (in-progress epic) — Level-scaled enemy counts / power-up drops; the level-scaling infrastructure (`levelScaling.ts`, F1 AH-0MVLJEE7O008RX9X) that this feature coordinates with.
- **AH-0MUI820PM0038HS2** (completed) — Harvester + data-driven multi-hit `health`; the seam this feature extends.
- **AH-0MUJRVYWG006NJUU** (completed) — Shared multi-hit kill finalisation / `takeDamage` seam.
- **AH-0MUJRVYJH00485YR** (completed) — Data-driven enemy health config (CSV codec + editor).
- **AH-0MTV7JOLU006W8PT** (completed) — Contact rule: player crashing into an enemy destroys both. **Extended by this item** (Q6 = B): a shielded enemy's field absorbs the ram (one field hit, both survive); unshielded enemies keep the original rule.
- **AH-0MVBKT2WO001AR14** (open) — Player Force Field feedback (distinct scope; do not conflate).
- **AH-0MV97RISJ002WR2S** (open) — Wave Laser limited hit power (piercing interplay; verify AOE/piercing behaviour against the field).
- Repo `AGENTS.md` — Gym↔game parity convention.

### Related work (automated report)

#### Related work items
- **AH-0MT7USMWN0071UF5** – Clarify enemy pass-through and bullet-blocking rules in GDD (Wall vs Dive Bomb) (completed)
- **AH-0MVBKT2WO001AR14** – More forcefield feedback (open)
- **AH-0MU7JTEY3004EXR2** – Show level/wave progress as 'Level N of 5, Wave M of K' (completed)

#### Repository file matches
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: destroyed, enemies, exposed, fields, force (+13 more); the enemy-build/health seams this feature extends
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: the GDD §2.6/§4.1 floor the "no shield layer" rule this item changes
- `README.md` — matched: broad gameplay terms; check for any shield/level claims on release

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption:** the three-field linear model (start level, start hits, max hits at L10) is the right "per-enemy curve variation" shape; operator confirmed per-enemy tunable start levels (some L2, others L3+) and "subtle variations of this curve for different enemies".
- **Assumption:** "killed in a single hit" after field break applies to the 1-HP majority; the Harvester keeps its 5 HP once its field is down (AC2, operator Q2 = A).
- **Assumption (confirmed, Q6 = B):** a shielded enemy's field also absorbs a player **contact/ram** — exactly one field hit is consumed and both sides survive the collision; the pre-existing rule (both destroyed, AH-0MTV7JOLU006W8PT) applies once the field is down.
- **Assumption (implementation detail, flagged):** "one field hit per ram" needs a re-arm so a sustained overlap cannot drain the whole field frame-by-frame. Proposed: a documented ram re-arm cooldown (~0.5 s) resolved once in the shared core; recorded as an OPEN QUESTION in the Appendix for the review gate.
- **Risk:** force fields stack with the level-scaling density/drop changes (epic AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P) and could push late levels into bullet-sink tedium; mitigated by the 5-hit cap, per-archetype defaults, and bot-batch survival evidence.
- **Risk:** heavy archetypes (Tank/Harvester) with fields at L2–3 may frustrate players who maxed weapons; mitigated by keeping light archetypes unshielded for longer and tuning via CSV.
- **Risk:** the gym slider for formation gyms bypasses the level curve, so an editor could author values the campaign never produces; documented divergence + editorial note in the gym panel.
- **Risk:** editing the CSV schema/editor touches shared tooling (codec, gym panel, docs tests); keep defaults `0` so existing rows and persisted blobs load unchanged.
- **Scope-creep guard:** no retuning of enemy health, weapon levels, drop rates or the player shield/force-field power-ups; separate items are created for any of those discovered during implementation.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers


- **Q6 — Should a shielded enemy absorb a player ram with its field, or is contact unchanged (both destroyed) as AC2 originally stated?** Options: (A) unchanged — ram destroys both regardless of field; (B) field absorbs the ram — one field hit is consumed and the player survives the collision; (C) field breaks entirely on ram, enemy survives, player destroyed. — **Answer (operator): B.** Source: interactive reply to the plan skill. A shielded enemy's field absorbs the ram: one field hit is consumed, the enemy survives and the player survives the collision. Once the field is down the original contact rule (both destroyed, AH-0MTV7JOLU006W8PT) applies. AC2 and the Risks section were rewritten accordingly. Precedent reused: Thorn Field's ram absorption (`tryConsumeThornsRam`) in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` step 4 of `_handleCollisions`.
- **OPEN QUESTION (Q6 follow-on, for the producer at the plan review gate):** how long is the ram re-arm after a field absorbs a ram? Without one, a held overlap consumes a field hit every frame and drains the field instantly. **Recommended:** a dedicated ~0.5 s shared re-arm constant (do *not* reuse the post-hit invulnerability window, which would also grant blink immunity). Directed to: Producer — affects feel and the field's effective durability against ramming.
- **Q1 — Which enemies gain a field, and how does it scale with level?** Options: (A) one global level curve for all regular ships; (B) per-archetype data-driven `forceFieldHits` in the enemy CSV/editor plus a level bonus; (C) level-scaled spawn chance with a small fixed field; (D) only heavy archetypes. — **Answer (operator): B — "start with a heavier getting stronger fields".** Source: interactive reply. Per-archetype base values, with heavier/larger archetypes (Tank, Harvester) entitled to stronger fields; the level curve strengthens them further.
- **Q2 — Does the field replace or stack on existing health?** Options: (A) separate layer — field absorbs N hits first, then normal `EnemyConfig.health` (Harvester keeps 5 HP); (B) the field replaces durability — one hit after break, even the Harvester; (C) merge field + health into a single bubble/total. — **Answer (operator): A.** Source: interactive reply. Field is an additive layer in front of existing data-driven health.
- **Q3 — How much feedback and balance evidence?** Options: (A) full — shared bubble (distinct from player's), absorb flash, break flash/cue, gym control to force fields, level-gym parity, bot-batch evidence at L1/L5/L10; (B) bubble + flash only, no audio, no bot batch; (C) minimal body tint instead of a bubble. — **Answer (operator): A.** Source: interactive reply. Full feedback surface and balance evidence.
- **Q4 — Should heavy archetypes show a field at level 1, or only from a start level?** Options: (A) fields appear only from a start depth (level-1 run untouched), with the level curve adding field hits past level 2; (B) heavy archetypes show base field hits from level 1. — **Answer (operator): "This needs to be tunable on a per enemy basis, so some will have shields from level 2, others level 3 or more."** Source: interactive reply. Per-archetype `forceFieldStartLevel`; no field at level 1 for any archetype by default; some archetypes start at level 2, others later.
- **Q5 — Confirm the concrete level curve (L1–2: 0, L3–4: +1, L5–6: +2, L7–8: +3, L9–10: +4, base per archetype, cap 5).** Options: (A) adopt table; (B) bases all 0; (C) different shape. — **Answer (operator): "See 1 (use subtle variations of this curve for different enemies)."** Source: interactive reply. Adopted a three-field linear model — `forceFieldStartLevel`, `forceFieldStartHits`, `forceFieldMaxHits` (at level 10), `clamp(round(lerp), 0, 5)` — giving each archetype a subtle per-enemy variation of the reference curve.
- **Open item carried to review (assumption, not yet confirmed):** enemy fields absorb only player **bullet** damage; player contact/ram behaviour is unchanged (both destroyed, AH-0MTV7JOLU006W8PT). If shields should absorb rams too, that is a product change to confirm during brief review.

data.description:
# Intake brief — What does Field of Thorns do? (AH-0MVJ8YKR70096C6T)

## Headline

The Thorn Field power-up (reported as "Field of Thorns") is fully wired but
invisible: it grants 2–6 free rams with no in-world feedback, and a hold-full
grant is spent after those rams once. Give it an obvious, visible presence —
a shared lime spiked aura around the ship, a distinct absorb burst when a ram
is used, and a recharge so the field keeps doing something all run.

## Problem statement

The Thorn Field upgrade appears to do nothing. The mechanics are wired
(AH-0MVH80ZJ7009W18Z): while armed, ramming an enemy destroys it without
costing a life, for a level-resolved budget of 2–6 rams. But there is no
in-world visual (no aura, no absorb feedback — only a small HUD row), and a
hold-full (permanent) grant gives a one-off budget that is inert once spent,
so the upgrade reads as dead weight.

## Users

- **Players** collecting Thorn Field drops and taking the hold-full "Thorn
  Field" permanent upgrade.

**User story:** "As a player, when I pick up the Thorn Field or take it as a
hold-full upgrade, I can see it has armed my ship, I can see each ram I absorb
work, and the field keeps re-arming so the upgrade stays meaningful."

## Acceptance Criteria

Measurable, testable.

- **Visible aura.** While the Thorn Field is armed (active with ≥ 1 ram
   charge), a lime spiked aura radiates from the ship in **PlayScene and every
   combat/power-up gym** (`GymPowerUpsCombat`, `GymFormationScene`),
   drawn through one shared helper in `src/scenes/core/CombatEffectVisuals.ts`
   (gym↔game parity). The aura reflects the remaining charge count (e.g.
   rotating spike count and/or intensity) and clears when the budget is spent
   or the window expires.
- **Absorb feedback.** When a ram is absorbed (`tryConsumeThornsRam()` →
   true in the shared ram branch), the enemy is destroyed as today **and** a
   distinct lime spike-shatter burst + cue fires at the collision, visibly
   different from a normal player hit. No absorb when the field is exhausted
   or inactive (rams hurt normally again).
- **Recharge (Q2=c).** The field regains one ram charge automatically on a
   level-resolved interval while active: a permanent (hold-full) field
   recharges for the whole run; a field-pickup window recharges while its
   window is still active, up to the level-resolved max budget. New
   `thornsRecharge` axis in `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS` (draft values — see
   assumptions).
- **HUD.** The existing `Thorn Field xN` row keeps showing remaining
   charges; for an armed field it also shows the recharge countdown (next ram
   in Ns). A permanent (hold-full) field that is mid-recharge at 0 charges
   also shows the countdown, so the row is never an inert bare label. Stacks
   and remaining values continue straight from the shared registry.
- **Documentation.** The GDD power-up table (§4.4.3, `docs/Game Design
   Document.md` row 920) gains the Thorn recharge axis; code comments and any
   related docs/README notes are updated.
- **Tests & parity.** Unit tests for the recharge clock and aura helper,
   regression tests for absorb feedback (game + gyms), the existing parity
   sweeps (`CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`, `powerUpLeveling.parity.test.ts`,
   `choicePool.parity.test.ts` and the equivalence/duplicate-body guard) stay
   green, and the full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- **gym↔game parity:** all visual and recharge behaviour lives once in the
  shared core (`src/scenes/core/`, shared `EffectsRegistry`) and is consumed
  by both the game and every gym — no divergent copies (AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1).
- **Mechanics scope:** the only mechanics change is the recharge (Q2=c).
  Ramming stays destroy-enemy-no-score; exhaust/expiry behaviour is unchanged.
- Visual-only for the aura (Q1=a): no passive contact damage.
- UK English; escape only backticks; no changes to `.pi/`, `skill/`,
  `command/` directories.
- Deterministic visuals (pure functions of registry state, frame-rate
  independent) so game, gyms and tests agree.

## Existing state

- `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE.thorns` = "Thorn Field" (`src/powerups/types.ts:251`),
  full level specs (`src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts:854-883`, thornsAbsorbs
  2→6, thornsDuration 8→16 s).
- Registry: `_thornsRemaining`, `thornsRemaining()`, `hasThornsRam()`,
  `tryConsumeThornsRam()`, expiry clears the budget
  (`src/powerups/effects.ts:391-397, 1060-1090`).
- Shared ram branch consumes the field (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts:1286-1298`).
- HUD row + stacks (`src/ui/HUD.ts:499-533`).
- No in-world visual exists for thorns; the shared visual seam is
  `src/scenes/core/CombatEffectVisuals.ts` (shield bubble, force-field
  bubble, phase ghost), called from `PlayScene`, `GymPowerUpsCombat`,
  `GymFormationScene`.

## Desired change

1. Add shared `drawThornsAura(graphics, player, registry)` + constants to
   `CombatEffectVisuals.ts` (neon-lime `ICON_COLORS.thorns` 0x99ff33 family,
   spiked halo echoing `drawThorns` in `src/powerups/icons.ts:562-583`).
2. Each of the three scenes owns a thorns graphics object, draws the aura in
   `_updateVisuals`/`_updateEffectVisuals` and clears it (mirrors the
   force-field bubble wiring).
3. Absorb feedback: the shared ram branch, when `tryConsumeThornsRam()`
   returns true, triggers a shared "thorn absorb" VFX/sound seam (spike
   shatter burst at the collision, distinct from `_hitPlayer` cue).
4. Recharge: new `thornsRecharge` level axis + registry recharge clock
   advanced in the shared `EffectsRegistry.tick`, refilling the budget one
   ram at a time (permanent grants: whole run; timed windows: while the
   window is active), capped at the level-resolved max.
5. HUD: recharge countdown for an armed field.
6. GDD row update; regression + parity tests.

## Key Files

- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — add recharge clock state, level-resolved
  `thornsRecharge` interval, advance in `tick()`, refill in
  `tryConsumeThornsRam` path; keep existing accessors.
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — add `thornsRecharge` axis to the `thorns`
  spec and the typed variable set (~line 1080).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatEffectVisuals.ts` — new shared `drawThornsAura`
  helper + constants (aura visual, spent/expiry clearing).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — shared ram branch: absorb feedback seam
  (burst/cue) when the field absorbs.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — thorns graphics object +
  `drawThornsAura` in the per-frame visuals; absorb burst spawn.
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — recharge countdown for an armed field.
- Tests: `src/powerups/effects.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatEffectVisuals.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.test.ts`,
  parity sweeps (`CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/powerUpLeveling.parity.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/choicePool.parity.test.ts`).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — Thorn Field row (line 920) gains the
  recharge axis.

## Related work

- **AH-0MVH80ZJ7009W18Z** (Some power-ups appear to do nothing, completed,
  v0.1.14) — wired the thorn rams into the shared combat core. This item is
  the visibility + recharge gap on top of it; partial overlap, rewritten to
  address only the differences (see Appendix Q1/Q2).
- **AH-0MVCRC1Q0007JAV1** (5 net-new power-ups, completed) — catalogue,
  level curves and registry for thorns.
- **AH-0MV1BIX1W006XF95** (force field reflector, completed) — the shared
  force-field bubble precedent for a per-scene graphics + shared draw helper.
- **AH-0MUAYB5HR001HDYC** (shield bubble ending fade) — shared visual
  continuity precedent; the aura should mirror its pure-function-of-state
  style.
- **AH-0MVI4KTD8000FBJ7** (power-ups in hull-full screen, completed) — thorns
  is in the hold-full pool; the permanent grant is what this item makes
  visible/useful.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (recharge values):** draft `thornsRecharge` axis — 12 s base →
  5 s cap, `linear-clamped`, k = -1, discrete (patterned on `strikeInterval`).
  Values are a starting point for implementer/balance review, not gospel.
- **Assumption (recharge scope):** recharge runs only while the field is
  armed (active). A spent one-off pickup window recharges within its window;
  a permanent grant recharges across the whole run. The clock stops when the
  window ends.
- **Assumption (visual semantics):** spike count/intensity maps to remaining
  charge count so the spent state is readable; exact proportions are
  implementer choice within the shared helper.
- **Risk:** scope creep toward a passive-contact-damage "field" — rejected
  (Q1=a); record as a separate item if wanted.
- **Risk:** aura confusion with Shield/Force Field bubbles — mitigate with
  the thorns lime colour + spike motif that already exist in the icon.
- **Risk:** parity drift if scenes hand-roll the aura — mitigated by the
  single shared helper and existing duplicate-body guards.
- **Risk:** recharge making Thorn Field too strong — cap the budget at the
  level-resolved max and floor the interval at 5 s.
- **Risk:** recharge regressing existing permanent-grant tests
  (`PlayScene.test.ts:7118`, `mineralLayer.test.ts:289`) — the recharge is
  additive on top of `applyCollect('thorns', true) → hasThornsRam()`, so the
  grant itself and the first absorptions must behave exactly as today.

## Related work (automated report — find-related)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVH80ZJ7009W18Z** – Some power-ups appear to do nothing (completed)
- **AH-0MVI4KTD8000FBJ7** – Not all power-ups are appearing in the hull-full screen (completed)
- **AH-0MUTPEHYW005YP3C** – Test: P10 timed field pickup and permanent stacking effects (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: appears, effect, field, needs, nothing, upgrade, visible
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: appears, effect, field, needs, nothing, upgrade, visible
- `docs/TELEMETRY.md` — matched: appears, effect, field, needs, nothing, upgrade, visible

> Full report persisted at `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-AH-0MVJ8YKR70096C6T.md`.

## Plan review notes (implementation guidance)

Recorded by the `plan` skill's automated review of this brief. These are
guidance additions only — goal, scope and acceptance criteria intent are
unchanged.

- **Reuse the existing recharge engine seam (reuse check).**
  `EffectsRegistry.tick(dt)` already forwards `dt` to
  `PowerUpLevelStore.tickRecharge(dt)` (`src/powerups/effects.ts:705`,
  AH-0MV82I8IL0012RXY AC1/AC5), which is the shared per-charge recharge clock
  the game and every gym advance identically. Two axis conventions already
  exist for recharge:
  - rate style — `phaseRechargeRate` / `teleportRechargeRate`, unit `/s`,
    `exponential-saturation` (the recharge axes' dominant convention, kept
    monotonic non-decreasing in charges/second);
  - interval style — `strikeInterval`, unit `s`, `linear-clamped`, `k = -1`
    (the draft `thornsRecharge` values in this brief).

  Whichever convention is chosen, the derived rate (`1 / interval`) must stay
  monotonic non-decreasing across levels (the invariant every existing
  interval axis documents), and the recharge clock must advance only on the
  shared `tick` path — never per-scene. Reusing the store's clock is preferred
  over a second parallel timer.
- **Test-first ordering.** Write the recharge-clock tests
  (`src/powerups/effects.test.ts`), the aura-helper tests
  (`src/scenes/core/CombatEffectVisuals.test.ts`) and the absorb-feedback
  regression tests (game + gyms) before wiring the scenes, so AC1–AC3 are
  observable before the visuals land.
- **No phasing decision.** This item is a single vertical slice (~22 h
  recommended effort, Low risk); it is small enough that splitting into
  sub-phases would add overhead without reducing risk. It is therefore planned
  as one slice with no child items: tests, shared core, scenes, HUD, docs and
  parity sweeps in one change.
- **Aura/absorb determinism.** Both helpers must be pure functions of registry
  state plus the frame clock handed in by the caller (mirroring the
  shield-bubble fade in AH-0MUAYB5HR001HDYC), so game, gyms and unit tests
  agree frame for frame.
- **Estimate currency.** The effort/risk report already on this item
  (Small effort, Low risk, 2026-10-24) predates only these guidance notes —
  scope is unchanged, so no re-estimate was run.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What should 'obvious and visible' mean?" — Answer (operator): **A —
  Visual-only**: lime spiked aura around the ship while armed, burst/flash +
  cue when a ram is absorbed; mechanics otherwise unchanged. Source:
  interactive reply.
- Q: "The permanent Thorn Field currently spends its 2 rams once and is inert
  for the rest of the run — in scope?" — Answer (operator): **C — recharge
  one ram on a timer** (level-resolved interval; see assumptions for draft
  values). Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Where must the effect apply?" — Answer (operator): **A — game and all
  gyms through the shared `CombatEffectVisuals` helper (parity)**. Source:
  interactive reply.
- Research: the thorns wiring landed in v0.1.14 (AH-0MVH80ZJ7009W18Z, commit
  154b7adb); no in-world visual exists today (only the HUD row,
  `src/ui/HUD.ts:499-533`); the shared visual seam and force-field precedent
  are in `src/scenes/core/CombatEffectVisuals.ts`.

# TDD red phase: pin the force-field contract before implementation

**Parent:** AH-0MVJ8W4GE007OMNT (enemy force fields scale with level).
**Slice:** test-first contract tests for the pure resolver and the config/CSV
codec. These tests are authored **before** any production code exists and are
expected to fail until the sibling item Force-field config and resolver (AH-0MVM8GRQ8006HGPK)
lands.

## Goal

As a developer, I want the force-field curve and the three new CSV columns
pinned by executable contracts, so the data model and resolver cannot drift
from AC1 while they are being built.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `src/core/enemyForceField.test.ts` (new) pins `enemyForceFieldHits(level, config)`:
  - returns `0` at level 1 for **every** shipped archetype (L1 untouched, AC1);
  - returns `0` for any level below `forceFieldStartLevel`, including
    `forceFieldStartLevel = 0` ("never shielded") at all levels;
  - equals `forceFieldStartHits` exactly at `forceFieldStartLevel`;
  - reaches `forceFieldMaxHits` at the campaign maximum level (10);
  - is monotonically non-decreasing between those two anchors, with
    `Math.round` (half-up) rounding at the midpoints;
  - is clamped to `[0, 5]` — `forceFieldMaxHits = 9` never yields more than 5;
  - is deterministic and never mutates the supplied config;
  - resolves `NaN`/non-numeric levels to level 1 and `±Infinity` to the
    campaign ends; a fractional level rounds before the curve is evaluated.
- `src/core/csv.test.ts` + `src/core/enemyConfig.test.ts` pin the codec:
  - `forceFieldStartLevel`, `forceFieldStartHits`, `forceFieldMaxHits` parse
    from `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` rows;
  - a row with the columns **absent** defaults to `0` / `1` / `1`
    (unshielded, backwards compatible);
  - export → import round-trips the three values exactly;
  - a persisted legacy config blob without the fields loads with the defaults;
  - malformed values (`''`, `'abc'`, negative, non-integer) fall back to the
    documented defaults defensively rather than producing `NaN`.
- The tests demonstrably fail before the implementation commit (record the red
  run in the work-item comment) and pass afterwards.
- No production code is changed by this item other than what is needed to make
  the test files compile.

## Key Files

- `src/core/enemyForceField.test.ts` — **new** contract suite.
- `src/core/csv.test.ts`, `src/core/enemyConfig.test.ts`,
  `src/core/configTypes.test.ts` — codec/default contracts.

# Data-driven force-field fields plus the pure resolver

**Parent:** AH-0MVJ8W4GE007OMNT (AC1).
**Depends on:** Resolver and codec contract tests (AH-0MVM8GQKI006B50M) (red contracts must exist first).

## Goal

As a balance engineer, I want per-archetype force-field strength to be
data-driven — which archetypes are shielded, from which level, and how the hit
count grows — so I can shape late-campaign difficulty from the CSV without
touching scene code.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `EnemyConfig` gains `forceFieldStartLevel` (campaign level at which the
  archetype first gains a field; `0` = never shielded),
  `forceFieldStartHits` (field hits when it appears) and `forceFieldMaxHits`
  (field hits at the campaign maximum level), each with JSDoc stating the
  neutral default — `0` / `1` / `1` — so **every existing enemy is unshielded
  at level 1** and the shipped campaign is behaviourally unchanged at L1.
- `src/core/csv.ts` numeric codec reads/writes the three columns; absent
  columns default to `0`/`1`/`1`; `src/core/configDefaults.ts` seeds the
  defaults; the CSV header comments document each column.
- `src/core/enemyForceField.ts` (**new**) exports a pure, Phaser-free
  `enemyForceFieldHits(level, config)` implementing
  `clamp(round(lerp(startHits @ startLevel → maxHits @ maxLevel)), 0, 5)`,
  documented with the formula and reusing `clampLevel` from the landed
  `src/core/levelScaling.ts` (AH-0MVLJEE7O008RX9X) for level clamping.
- Shipped CSV rows carry per-archetype values with **subtle curve variations**
  (Q5): heavier archetypes (Tank, Harvester) get higher `forceFieldStartHits`
  /`forceFieldMaxHits` than light ones; start levels vary per archetype
  (some L2, others L3+); no archetype is shielded at L1.
- The red contract tests from the sibling test item go green; existing
  `csv`/`config`/`configStore` suites stay green; persisted blobs still load.
- Resolver is deterministic: same level + config ⇒ identical value.

## Documented assumptions

- Field strength is a pure function of `(level, config)` — no RNG.
- The campaign maximum level is 10 (`DEFAULT_LEVEL_SCALING_MAX_LEVEL`).

## Key Files

- `src/core/configTypes.ts` — `EnemyConfig` fields.
- `src/core/configDefaults.ts`, `src/core/configStore.ts`,
  `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` — defaults, persisted-blob compatibility, rows.
- `src/core/csv.ts` — numeric codec + header comments.
- `src/core/enemyForceField.ts` — **new** resolver.

# TDD red phase: pin entity absorb/break and the ram rule

**Parent:** AH-0MVJ8W4GE007OMNT (AC2).
**Depends on:** Force-field config and resolver (AH-0MVM8GRQ8006HGPK) (needs the resolved hit count).
**Blocks:** Entity force-field layer (AH-0MVM8GUZG008AWSU).

## Goal

As a developer, I want the absorb-before-hull, break-once and ram-absorb
semantics pinned by tests before they are implemented, so every damage source
keeps routing through the single shared `takeDamage()` seam.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.test.ts` pins:
  - an enemy built with `N` field hits exposes the remaining field hits;
  - `takeDamage()` while the field is up decrements the field and leaves
    `health` **unchanged**, reporting the hit as absorbed (distinct from a hull
    hit) so scenes can give different feedback;
  - the break (field reaching 0) is signalled **exactly once** and never again;
  - after the break the next hit decrements `health` as today — the 1-HP
    majority dies on that hit, the 5-HP Harvester still needs 5;
  - an enemy constructed with **no** field hits behaves exactly as before
    (backwards-compatible default), and `health` is still the only thing a ram
    or bullet touches for unshielded enemies.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.test.ts` pins the ram rule (Q6 = B): ramming a
  **shielded** enemy consumes exactly one field hit, destroys **neither** side
  and does not call `onPlayerHit`/`_hitPlayer`; ramming an **unshielded** enemy
  keeps today's both-destroyed behaviour; a second ram inside the re-arm window
  consumes nothing; Thorn Field keeps precedence and its own cue.
- `src/entities/enemyFactory.test.ts` pins that the effective field hit count
  is threaded from config into the constructed entity.
- Tests demonstrably fail before the implementation item lands (record the red
  run in a comment).

## Key Files

- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.test.ts`, `src/entities/Harvester.test.ts`.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.test.ts` — ram-absorb contract.
- `src/entities/enemyFactory.test.ts` — threading contract.

# Field absorbs hits (and rams) before the hull

**Parent:** AH-0MVJ8W4GE007OMNT (AC2).
**Depends on:** Entity field and ram contract tests (AH-0MVM8GTG7002IRTL).

## Goal

As a player, I want a shielded enemy to absorb a few hits behind a barrier
before the ship inside is exposed, so late-game firepower is challenged again
and the barrier-then-hull read is intuitive.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `BaseEnemy` holds field state (remaining hits), decrements it in
  `takeDamage()` **before** `health`, signals the break exactly once and only
  then lets `health` take damage — no parallel damage path.
- Every player damage source routes through that seam and depletes the field:
  normal bullet, piercing (Wave Laser), AOE weapons, Smart Bomb, Orbital
  Strike, Frenzy bonus hits. A parameterised test asserts at least one case per
  source. Each absorbed hit still **consumes the bullet** (today's behaviour)
  and only the field changes — `health` is untouched until the break.
- Player contact/ram (Q6 = **B**): a shielded enemy's field absorbs the ram —
  exactly **one** field hit per contact, the enemy survives and the player
  survives (no `_hitPlayer`). Implemented once in the shared
  `CombatScene._handleCollisions` step 4, mirroring the Thorn Field
  `tryConsumeThornsRam` precedent, guarded by a documented **shared re-arm**
  constant (recommended ~0.5 s; OPEN QUESTION Q6a in the parent) so a sustained
  overlap cannot drain the field frame-by-frame. Once the field is down the
  existing both-destroyed rule applies unchanged.
- `enemyFactory` threads the resolved hit count into the entity; constructing
  without a field is byte-for-byte today's behaviour.
- `health`, weapon levels, drop rates and the player Shield/Force Field
  power-ups are untouched.

## Key Files

- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts`, `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts`.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — ram-absorb branch + shared re-arm
  (shared core: the game and every gym inherit it).
- `src/core/constants.ts` — ram re-arm / field constants if not colocated.
